newsitem.title: USA: Over 100 lawyers back pay-to-play ban -- SEC chief.
newsitem.headline: Over 100 lawyers back pay-to-play ban -- SEC chief.

text.p: SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt on Wednesday said the number of prominent lawyers nationwide that have signed a resolution to ban "pay-to-play" has more than tripled, from 30 to over 100.
Levitt, who released the list of attorneys at a press briefing, added that deans of 47 American law schools, including Columbia, Harvard and Yale, also have called for an end to the practice.
Levitt issued the list less that one week before American Bar Association delegates meeting in San Francisco are scheduled to consider a pay-to-play policy resolution.
The draft policy would condemn pay-to-play among lawyers and calls for a task force to study whether a ban is needed.

"Throughout our history, leaders have emerged from America's legal community to mobilize lawyers for needed reform," Levitt said. "I am encouraged that so many of our country's distinguished law school deans, leading lawyers and devoted public servants have followed this tradition and called for an end to pay-to-play."
Levitt said: "This odious practice has tainted our municipal bond market as well as the reputation of many good lawyers."
"Next week, I will ask the American Bar Association to join this effort and bring an end to pay-to-play," Levitt said.
Levitt recently announced the formation of a prestigious panel called Lawyers Committee to End Pay-to-Play, headed by Judge William Webster.
Levitt wants bond lawyers to follow the lead of the Association of the Bar of the City of New York, which last year called for an all-out ban on lawyers pay-to-play.
Pay-to-play refers to muni bond professionals who give contributions to elected state and local officials in return for bond business, or even to be placed in the running for such business.

Judge Webster said, "Pay-to-play brings discredit upon the legal profession. The ABA and state bar associations and disciplinary bodies can and should take steps to bring this practice to an end. We hope they will respond to our call."
